name: TX-14
label: Likely R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a PVI of R+12
Weber is an incumbent with a large fundraising advantage
Bartie has raised almost nothing and is out of cash
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Weber: a heavily Republican district, incumbency, and a dominant money edge over a Democratic challenger who has raised under $30,000 and holds negative cash. Markets price this as a near-certain Republican hold, and nothing in the evidence suggests movement toward Bartie.
model.watch: Any late polling or surge in Democratic outside spending could narrow the margin, though a Weber loss remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Randy Weber seeks another term in this southeastern Texas district, which leans Republican by twelve points at the presidential level. He enters the general election as a well-funded incumbent, with roughly $920,000 on hand and modest outside support, and no organized outside opposition targeting him.

Challenger Thurman Bartie has run a minimal campaign, raising about $27,000 and ending the period with negative cash on hand. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Weber about a 95 percent chance of winning. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and the fundraising gap makes this a Safe Republican seat.
